## Ongoing Data Access Efforts Independent of OPR

To support OPR community data access and processing, CReSIS maintains 3 PB of active storage backed up to LTO tape storage. Tiered active storage is connected via 40, 80, and 160 Gbps network connections to an exclusive-use computer cluster with 1584 cores. The cluster includes 32 compute-nodes and 10 head-nodes for processing. Head nodes support graphical remote desktop session management software. The Linux GPU processing nodes are equipped with four Nvidia A5000, one Nvidia A6000, and two Nvidia L40S GPUs. In addition, there are 4 Windows Servers and core servers running support services. Storage is available on Globus, https, ftp, and ssh.

Email opr@openpolarradar.org for an external account.

OPR data providers and data volumes

OPR is global in scope and seeks to involve radioglaciology domain scientists, AI data scientists, and the software and data engineers behind the various satellite, airborne, and ground-based ice penetrating radar data collected over ice sheets, mountain glaciers, sea ice, and planetary icy bodies.

The initial effort is focusing on the datasets collected by the Alfred Wegener Institute (AWI), British Antarctic Survey (BAS), Center for Remote Sensing and Integrated Systems (CReSIS), Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory (LDEO), University of Texas Institute for Geophysics (UTIG), and the University of Washington (UW).

Data upload status: AWI is 100%; BAS is ~60% (copy in progress); CReSIS is 100%; LDEO is 100%; UTIG is ~100% (filling in missing files as the data are ingested); UW is ~0% (focusing on this in 2026).

C41G-1101 Data access tools for polar radar sounder data: Enabling reproducible workflows for Open Polar Radar data Thomas Teisberg1, Shane Grigsby1, John Paden2 and Reece Mathews2, (1) Astera Institute, Emeryville, United States, (2) Center for Remote Sensing and Integrated Systems (CReSIS), University of Kansas, Lawrence, United States

Thursday, 18 December 2025

08:30 - 12:00 •Hall EFG (Poster Hall) (NOLA CC)

Abstract: Open Polar Radar (OPR) is a multi-institution organization whose goal is to provide unified data processing tools, products, and access for over 3.5 million line-km of radar sounder data. Over 1.4 million line-km of data are currently available, with access provided through the OPR geoportal and web interface, a STAC catalog, and the xOPR Python library. Efforts are underway to process the remaining archival radar sounder data using the open-source OPR tools . Raw data, unfocused radargrams, focused radargrams, and bed and surface picks generated from these data are available in common data formats. Access to these datasets is possible through web-based tools and programmatically in both Python and Matlab, enabling more reproducible workflows in polar science. Here, we provide updates on the state of tool development and data processing within OPR.

Membership in OPR is open and organizations working with or producing radar sounder data are encouraged to join.

# Search

Open Polar Radar includes a Javascript geoportal and a Matlab geoportal for searching and viewing data products connected to a geospatial database with a web portal at https://openpolarradar.org. The geoportal includes 1. a WMS and WFS based on the open-source

GeoServer package. 2. a geospatial database based on the open-source

PostgreSQL database with the PostGIS geospatial extension. 3. an open source Django REST API These services all run on an open-source Apache web server. A block diagram of the spatial data infrastructure is shown blow.

## Polarimetric Processing

A polarimetric processing pipeline has been added to the Open Polar Radar toolbox. Examples from a recent ground campaign are shown to the right. The unwrapped interferometric phase (VV - HH) shown on the left is constructed from an along-flow line data product. The unwrapped phase shown on the right is constructed from a cross-track flow line adjacent to the result on the left. Steps:

1. Synthesize images from 0-180 deg antenna rotation 2. Select a synthesis angle and synthesize the result 3. Apply correlation based coregistration 4. Form interferogram from coregistered images 5. Smooth image 6. Phase unwrap with SNAPHU

During the past year, we have focused on data processing the:

1. BAS PASIN data – Equalization routines for receiver time and phase variation versus slow time

have been developed. These were needed to ensure phase coherence during array processing. 2. UTIG HICARS data – All steps are complete except final quality control for four seasons in East

Antarctica. 3. LDEO DICE data – All steps are complete except final quality control for the three seasons over

the Ross Ice Shelf.

In an independent effort, AWI has released their land ice data in a common NetCDF data format and made this data available to OPR. The old sounder data uses an incoherent (power detected) digital system. OPR will directly ingest these NetCDF files rather than the raw data files since there is limited processing that can be done on incoherent data. The new sounder data uses the Open Polar Radar toolbox and these data products can be directly ingested.

# Multipass Processing

The multipass processing pipeline in the Open Polar Radar toolbox has been updated with improved coregistration and more robust error checking. Processing steps:

1. Coregister flights using dead reckoning (GNSS and INS) 2. Coregister images with data dependent cross correlation 3. Form interferograms to estimate the equalization coefficients 4. Compensate for the spatial baseline using the cross-track slope 5. Perform array processing and interferometric processing on the resultant images (e.g. crosstrack slope estimation, swath imaging, vertical velocity)

Multipass processing works with both single look complex SAR images and with array processed images.
